examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}に{行|い}きます。
{会社|かいしゃ}は{何時|なんじ}からですか？
どんな{会社|かいしゃ}で{働|はたら}いていますか？
examples.english: What kind of company do you work at?

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{大|おお}きい{会社|かいしゃ}で{仕事|しごと}をしていて、{毎日|まいにち}{忙|いそが}しいです。
examples.english: My father works at a big company and is busy every day.

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}を{出|で}たら、{日本|にほん}の{会社|かいしゃ}に{入|はい}って、{海外|かいがい}で{働|はたら}きたいと{思|おも}っています。
examples.english: After graduating from university, I want to join a Japanese company and work overseas.

notes:
{会社|かいしゃ} means company or corporation, and also refers to one's workplace.

KANJI:
{会|かい} (meeting) + {社|しゃ} (shrine/company) - an organization where people meet to work.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {会社|かいしゃ}に{行|い}く: to go to work (lit. "go to the company")
- {会社|かいしゃ}を{辞|や}める: to quit one's job
- {会社|かいしゃ}に{入|はい}る: to join a company

RELATED WORDS:
- {会社員|かいしゃいん}: company employee, office worker
- {株式|かぶしき}{会社|がいしゃ}: stock company (often abbreviated as {株|かぶ})
- {有限|ゆうげん}{会社|がいしゃ}: limited company

USAGE:
{会社|かいしゃ}に{行|い}く can mean both "going to the company (building)" and "going to work" depending on context.
